newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes lower on U.S. dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes lower on U.S. dollar strength.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed softer against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday despite the central bank's early effort to support the local currency, dealers said.
The local unit closed at T$28.656 against Tuesday's T$28.625 finish.
Turnover through dealers was active at US$310.5 million.
The Taiwan dollar rose to an intra-day high of T$28.550 in early session in what some dealers suspected was intervention orchestrated by the central bank.
Other dealers said a tight Taiwan dollar liquidity in the banking system and inflows of foreign equity funds also helped push the Taiwan dollar higher in morning trade.
But in the afternoon, waves of U.S. dollar buying -- some in the form of non-delivery forward trading -- emerged to pull the rate to a lower close, dealers said.
"The U.S. dollar demand is still very heavy due to the greenback's persistent strength overseas," said one dealer.
Another dealer said the central bank would allow a slow and gradual Taiwan dollar slide.
"The central bank did not want to see a sharp depreciation, but it's likely to keep its hands off as long as the Taiwan dollar depreciation comes slowly and gradually," the second dealer said.
A range of T$28.60-70 was seen for Thursday.
